subject.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `models auth clear-cooldown <profile-id>` as the supported explicit recovery contract, and is terminal-plus-safe-restart recovery sufficient for affected users?
rationale: The implementation can be judged mechanically, but selecting a permanent public CLI contract versus automatic or guided recovery requires maintainer product intent.

options.title: Adopt and prove the escape hatch
options.body: Approve the profile-scoped command as an operator recovery action, require inspectable end-to-end proof, and retain guided recovery as the desired user-facing end state.

options.title: Move recovery to Doctor or UI
options.body: Pause this command and expose the same authoritative reset through a guided Doctor/Fix or in-product recovery flow.

options.title: Rely on automatic recovery
options.body: Close this PR if provider-specific probes and fallback policy should be the only supported early-recovery mechanism.

recommendation.title: Adopt and prove the escape hatch
recommendation.body: Approve the profile-scoped command as an operator recovery action, require inspectable end-to-end proof, and retain guided recovery as the desired user-facing end state.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal combines major auth-profile invariant work with merger responsibility for related cooldown corrections.
